evidence: web-host.lisp:120 (setq reply (concatenate 'fnn-octets reply part)) runs once per render quantum. web-host.lisp:112-113 (if (eq (first results) :defer) (sleep (/ (min (second results) 1000) 1000)) loops with no deadline. The header (27-28) claims "the whole request within fn-web-host-request-seconds", but the deadline built at 209 is passed only to fnn-web-read-request.
fix: Stream each quantum to the socket as it is rendered, which ACL2 already frames per quantum, or collect the parts and join them once. Carry the request deadline into fnn-web-feed and stop, closing the session, when it expires.

reviewer: web-host.lisp:120 concatenates the whole accumulated reply once per render quantum, which is O(N*Q) copying, and the full reply is held in memory before fnn-web-fill. The :defer loop (112-113) and the yield sleeps (124-125) have no deadline; the deadline built at 209 goes only to fnn-web-read-request. The accept loop (web-host.lisp:318-323) serves one connection at a time in the single 'fn web face' thread, so one slow or repeatedly deferred request blocks every other browser.
scenario: A browser asks for a large article or a long group listing. Each render quantum copies the whole accumulated reply again, so a reply of N octets in Q quanta costs O(N*Q) copying, and the full reply sits in memory before any byte is written (D27: bound work, not data). One face thread serves every connection, so a single such request, or a session the owner keeps deferring (login pacing, gate pressure), stalls the whole web face past the advertised request window with no timeout.
title: Web reply is buffered whole with quadratic concatenation, and the feed has no deadline despite the per-request time claim
